additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia nervosa is characterized by recurrent episodes of eating unusually large amounts of food in a discrete period, accompanied by a sense of loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as self‑induced vomiting, misuse of laxatives or diuretics, fasting, or excessive exercise to prevent weight gain. Individuals typically have an overvaluation of weight and shape, but unlike anorexia nervosa, they usually maintain body weight in the normal or slightly above-normal range. The course is often chronic or relapsing, with symptoms waxing and waning in response to stress, changes in life circumstances, and mood or anxiety states. It is distinguished from binge-eating disorder by the presence of recurrent compensatory behaviors and from normal dieting or overeating by the degree of loss of control, frequency, and the centrality of body image concerns in self‑evaluation.

patient.personality: Lorian is a meticulous, community‑minded organizer who channels creativity and care for others into structured projects and mentoring across generations.
patient.stressor: Around 17 months ago, Lorian’s long, difficult separation from her spouse became final, coinciding with her decision to step back from a leadership role in her community arts nonprofit and spend more time alone at home. The abrupt shift from a structured schedule filled with events, volunteers, and church music outreach to unstructured days intensified her focus on her body and aging, especially as she sorted old photos and family stories that reminded her of how she used to look. As she tried to regain a sense of control during this emotionally disorienting period, she began swinging between using food for comfort in the evenings and then resorting to increasingly drastic, secretive methods to "fix" what she feared it was doing to her body, all while maintaining a polished, composed presence at church and community gatherings. Over time, the shame, physical strain, and the amount of planning her eating and compensatory behaviors required started to interfere with her ability to enjoy painting, gardening, and mentoring younger artists, and a concerned church friend finally persuaded her to speak with a psychiatrist after Lorian tearfully admitted she was doing dangerous things to "get rid of" what she ate.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve started doing harmful things to get rid of food after I eat because I’m so afraid of gaining weight.”

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: Even though people tell me I’m slim for my age, every time I see an old photo of myself or catch my reflection in the bathroom mirror I’m gripped by this awful panic that if I’m not extremely careful I’ll suddenly balloon up and become this frumpy, invisible old woman no one recognizes from the vibrant person I used to be on stage at church or running the art center.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: On the mornings after a bad night of eating, I punish myself by skipping breakfast and sometimes lunch, drinking only tea and forcing myself to walk laps around the neighborhood or up and down the stairs until my knees ache, telling myself I don’t deserve to sit and paint or rest until I’ve burned off every bite.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: Most nights, after I’ve eaten too much alone in the kitchen, I stand over the bathroom sink with the fan on and the water running so no one can hear me, forcing myself to throw up or taking extra laxatives from the medicine cabinet, even when my throat burns and my stomach cramps, because I feel like I have to get all that food out of me right away or I’ll wake up fatter in the morning.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: When the house is quiet in the evenings I’ll start with a small snack, and before I know it I’ve gone through half a loaf of bread with butter, a full carton of ice cream, leftover casserole, and whatever else is in the fridge, eating standing up at the counter as if I have to finish it all before anyone walks in, even though I live alone now and I’m not even truly hungry.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: During those episodes it feels like a switch flips in my brain—some sensible part of me is begging, ‘Lorian, stop, you’re going to make yourself sick,’ but my hands just keep reaching for more food and I shovel it in so fast that it’s like I’m watching someone else do it and I can’t make her put the fork down.
